fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Rediscovering a Language of Numbers", "body": "Derek Tikkuri tells Chance that he built the Gematrinator website in January 2017, after meeting gematria through a source he names as Zach Hubbard. He was skeptical at first, since numerology seemed out there to him, so he built spreadsheets and analyzed the gematria of calendar dates, numbers and the Bible. He concluded it was relevant and ran a lot deeper than what he was learning at the time. Derek says he promised himself he would stop once he quit learning, and four or five years on he is still learning every day."}, {"title": "Decoding the News Before It Breaks", "body": "Derek argues that gematria earns its place because it lets decoders get ahead of events, claiming his community now explains news stories before they unfold instead of only in hindsight. He says he saw a society-changing event coming in 2020 and guessed it would start in Seattle, though he admits he did not know it would be a pandemic. He also concedes the method still needs work, plans to build a stronger database of these riddles, and asks aloud whether it is already too late."}, {"title": "Censorship, Fact Checkers and Platforms", "body": "Chance describes posting a short clip in which, as he tells it, a pharmacist unfolds a blank insert from a sealed box of the shots, and says it drew a fact-check label claiming only one insert in the whole carton carried printed information. He reads such labels as pressure that makes dissenting creators look like hoaxers. Derek says his first YouTube channel was deleted in 2018 yet he has not had a strike since, and he wonders whether that quiet means he is no longer touching what needs touching. Chance points to Rockfin for bonus content without the constant thumb of censorship, while Derek weighs a Patreon or Rockfin page."}, {"title": "Cash, Crypto and Control", "body": "Derek says he is wary of the crypto boom, pointing to Pirate Chain's sudden jump after a promotion and arguing that nobody profits unless others lose. He prefers cash for a practical reason: if a gas station attendant refuses service, he can still leave dollars on the counter, whereas a purely electronic currency could be switched off, which he says people should be deathly terrified of. Chance shares the worry, naming a cutoff from the economy people have been made dependent on as the thing to fear most, and riffs on a so-called Gov coin he says was announced."}, {"title": "Organic Synchronicity or Forced Encoding", "body": "Chance cautions that gematria should not be taken super seriously, and that high pattern recognition is both a blessing and a double edged sword in an age of constant psyops. Derek replies that a decoder should make the logical connection first, learn what counts as coincidence, and favor four digit matches over small reduction numbers, while Chance notes that longer matches stray further from random. Derek adds that he believes numerology points beyond five sense reality, that people are here for a reason, and that he no longer feels obligated to save everybody."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Derek Tikkuri, aka Gematrinator, returns for another round of InnerVerse deep dives and digital decodes!

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Energy Vampires and the Vaccine Divide", "body": "Chance recounts a park encounter with a stranger he reads as a textbook energy vampire, one who approaches from behind, flatters, then flips the mood the moment he voices doubt about vaccines, leaving him to ground himself afterward. Derek offers a theory that many people lack a true general purpose, and that the pandemic handed them a chance to feel they are making a difference by putting others down. He adds that he is disappointed so many people he tried to help do not want help, and that he has weighed a move abroad."}, {"title": "The Arch, the Eclipse and a Blackout", "body": "Derek says St. Louis became a favorite riddle of his year, linking the Gateway Arch to the annular eclipse of June 10, which he notes falls 54 years to the day after the arch opened, with the number 54 recurring in sun, arch and baseball. He reads a May 3 blackout at a Cardinals game in the arch's shadow as an intentional eclipse tribute, and shows how he mines the Five Millennium Canon for eclipse data. Chance adds that priestcraft may once have used predicted eclipses against people who lacked that knowledge."}, {"title": "Revelation, Jesuits and Eclipse Numbers", "body": "Derek argues that this year's twin eclipses and the book of Revelation line up, saying Revelation 6:12, which he calls the only Revelation verse naming both a solar and a lunar eclipse, sums to 1331, which he calls his major eclipse number. He sees a rise of the Jesuits, from Pope Francis to Gonzaga reaching the NCAA final, as part of the same pattern, and walks through numbers he ties to coach Mark Few and Revelation 3:2. Chance calls the connections mind blowing and says the numbers speak for themselves."}, {"title": "Minds, Language and the Unseen", "body": "Chance argues that scripture and high art can be read accurately through many lenses because things divinely inspired come from the realm of cause rather than effect, and says all of this demonstrates the hermetic principle of mentalism, that external reality originates in mind. Derek answers that numerology manifests because it exists only in our minds, like the agreed rules of a game, and suggests language itself may be numbers used to program ideas into one another. He says he fully believes forces work in the unseen and treats numerology as evidence, while Chance muses that technology may be an entryway."}, {"title": "Betting, Honesty and What Comes Next", "body": "Chance warns about the unhealthy side of obsessing over patterns and treating betting as a sure thing, and Derek answers that Vegas wins and that a code may be changed once too many people bet on it. He says he will track his own record if he ever makes picks, and that numerology will enrich a life, not necessarily a pocketbook. Looking ahead, Derek says dates such as 33 days after the coming lunar eclipse are worth watching for something big, while Chance raises a possible cyber false flag and relays a chat rumor of alien disclosure, which Derek allows might happen."}]
